summary.text: Every network gates participation behind a signed agreement, and only Visa publishes the application steps for a direct licence. Mastercard exposes its application form, and American Express and Discover route prospects to a representative or contact form.

Most partners never join directly. ISOs, payment facilitators, ATM deployers, programme managers and small issuers enter through a sponsor bank or principal that registers them and carries their liability.
Third-party registration is the sponsor's paperwork. The routes are Visa Program Request Management, Mastercard My Company Manager, and OptBlue registration forms emailed to American Express.
Due diligence is pushed down the chain. Networks require the sponsor to vet financials, principals and PCI status, and sometimes to visit the site, before registering an agent.
Identifiers arrive as a set at approval. Visa gives a temporary UVID and then a Business ID. American Express assigns participant number ranges, and Mastercard ties each ICA and BIN to a country.

Joining fees are mostly unpublished. The exceptions are Visa's 2016 agent fees, the American Express active BIN rental fee, no-fee OptBlue and AMEX Enabled registration, and Mastercard's high-risk licence fee.
Published service levels for joining steps are rare. PULSE promises portal credentials within five business days, and Mastercom and Mastercard Send publish onboarding durations.
Visa's 2016 agent FAQ gave five to seven business days per registration case. The study found no licensing timeline from any of the four networks.
At the partner, joining work sits with sponsorship oversight analysts, BIN sponsorship programme managers and network relationship leads. Postings describe it as case work tracked in Excel.
Card numbers trace to the ABA, which registers one IIN per legal entity under ISO/IEC 7812. Networks then license BINs to members, one licensee per BIN.
The Discover family's public door is a set of contact forms plus EASI self-registration. Diners Club licensing runs through a brand mailbox. PULSE publishes no sponsor or application process.

how_it_works.text: A regional licensing team first confirms eligibility. The applicant then gets Visa Access credentials and completes the application in the Client Lifecycle Management Tool.
During review the organisation holds a temporary UVID. A final Business ID is issued on approval.
Visa reviews regulatory permissions, AML and ATF programmes with a compliance questionnaire, credit and settlement risk, and risk management. The settlement review repeats every year.
A Principal licenses and uses only its own BIN. Each BIN has exactly one licensee, which answers for all activity on it and pays the numeric ID fees.
Within 10 business days of a BIN going live, the member enters contacts in the Client Directory on Visa Access. These name a Directory Manager, Primary Center Manager and Senior Officer.
Brand use sits under the Visa-owned marks licence. Visa may ask to review any branded material, and Europe requires a card design self-certification form.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Access, Client Lifecycle Management Tool
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where the licence application is completed after eligibility is confirmed, with a temporary UVID shown during review.

tools_and_screens.name: Client Directory (Client Service Provider Directory and My Organization's Contacts modules)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Member contacts and named roles, due within 10 business days of a BIN or BID implementation.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Partner account and Universal Login
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: One identity across Visa Developer, Visa Partner programmes and Visa Online, with extra validation for Visa Online.

friction.text: Eligibility rules live in charter documents outside the public rulebook, so an applicant cannot self-assess before contacting Visa.
Principal service fees and any licensing timeline are unpublished.
Several partner pages still name Visa Online after its rename to Visa Access, which leaves two names for one portal.

how_it_works.text: An applicant must be a regulated financial institution with an acceptable business plan. Mastercard admits applicants at its sole discretion and alone decides Principal or Affiliate status.
The application is the public Universal Onboarding Template, form 1400, titled an application for the licence to use Mastercard service marks.
AML and sanctions programmes are a licence condition. Named compliance contacts are kept in My Company Manager.
Mastercard may demand capital, collateral or escrow. It may also let an applicant operate on an interim basis while the application is pending.
Each customer receives an ICA. The ICA and BIN must reflect the country of activity within the licensed Area of Use, and adding a country means a new application.
Connect access for a new company starts with the Mastercard Connect Access Form, 1145 or 1145b, obtained from a representative.

tools_and_screens.name: Universal Onboarding Template, form 1400
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A public Qualtrics form for a new licensed customer application.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect, My Company Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Company records, contacts per ICA, AML and sanctions contacts, and service provider registration.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect sign-up
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A three-step request that ends with approval by the applicant company's own administrator.

friction.text: The live rulebook and brand pages refuse automated fetches, and the old public licensing guide survives only as a legacy page.
Joining and registration fees sit in the Pricing and Billing Center behind Connect.

how_it_works.text: There is no public application. Rulebooks are handed over only after an agreement is signed.
The first eligibility rule is a Participant Agreement that authorises issuing under assigned BIN ranges.
Bank partners must pass capital and soundness tests and hold an investment-grade rating, or post a guarantee, letter of credit or cash collateral.
Before launch American Express certifies specifications and assigns settlement parameters, currency code and participant number ranges. It also works with the partner's marketing agency.
A site survey, vulnerability scanning and any required site review come before beta test.
Participants are classed as Network Card License issuers, Independent Operators or Joint Ventures. Fees are negotiated bilaterally in each agreement.
Brand use runs under a Trademark Licensing Agreement. Issuers pay a monthly rental fee for each active BIN, USD 175 in the 2023 manual.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated home for manuals, the Participant Directory and Service Enrollment for network services after licensing.

tools_and_screens.name: Navigator training via Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Mandatory training before staff reach FraudNet, Network Disputes Manager and Program Progress Report.

tools_and_screens.name: User access forms and online enrolment
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Per-person system access, with business justification and manager approval, coordinated by the AEGNS Operations Manager.

friction.text: Obligations cannot be read before signing because the policy manual is confidential.
The public contact route is a web form that returns a case number, with no phone or email published.

how_it_works.text: Discover describes network partner agreements with financial institutions, fintechs and alliance networks. Prospects use a nine-category contact form.
The partnering page offers consultation with no steps, fees or timelines.
Diners Club issuers hold a Network Participation Agreement or a sublicence NPA. Prospects email a brand mailbox.
The Partner Product Portal's Going Live flow has five stages: Organization Identification, Legal and Risk Documentation, Configuration, Certification, and End to End Testing.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover Partner Product Portal, Going Live
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Five named onboarding stages seen in the site's code. The page renders only client side.

tools_and_screens.name: Diners Club issuer resources on ServiceNow
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Assets and tools for current Diners issuers only.

friction.text: Operating rules and specifications sit behind the Service Center login, with no public rulebook.
Diners Club issuer interchange is negotiated per issuer, with no published schedule.

best_pattern.text: Visa's licensing page publishes four steps, the review criteria and the identifier a partner holds during review. It is the clearest public map of a direct licence.

discover_today.text: Discover routes issuers to a contact form or a Diners brand mailbox. Its five-stage Going Live structure exists in code but is not visible as a readable page.

by_partner.partner_type: Issuers: community banks and credit unions (sponsored or associate)

how_it_works.text: Associate clients, typically smaller credit unions, hold their own licence and BIN. A Principal sponsors them for settlement, reporting and fees.
An Associate either licenses its own BIN, with one sponsor only since 2017, or uses a unique BIN licensed to its Principal. A Participant-type member cannot license a BIN.
Industry bodies can act as the Principal. ICBA Payments is a Visa principal that runs sponsored programmes and sells network sponsorship in a debit bundle.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Access, Client Lifecycle Management Tool
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The same licence application path as for principals.

friction.text: The sponsor carries liability for information on the Associate's BINs, which pushes risk review onto the sponsoring bank.

how_it_works.text: In the US an Affiliate can join through a Principal, an Association or a Type I processor. Mastercard stopped designating new Type I processors in May 2025.
The sponsor is liable to Mastercard for everything its sponsored affiliates do.

tools_and_screens.name: My Company Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The Principal maintains contacts for itself and each sponsored affiliate per ICA.

friction.text: The processor sponsorship route that many small issuers used is closed to new entrants.

how_it_works.text: The study found no public route for a US community bank or credit union to issue directly on American Express. The fintech route runs through sponsor banks on the Agile Partner Platform.

friction.text: American Express publishes no licensing tiers below a full participant.

how_it_works.text: PULSE participating institutions sign participation agreements that usually auto-renew. They pay participation and membership fees on top of switch fees.
Discover Debit is sold to regional banks and credit unions on an all-in programme fee, but the amount is not disclosed.
The PULSE website asks new users to register and promises credentials within five business days.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE secure website registration
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A three-step form: submit registration, receive a User ID within five business days, then reset the password.

friction.text: PULSE's public join path is a sales call-back form. No membership types, sponsor model or fees are published.
PULSE says it starts delivering services once the contract is signed, so the pre-contract experience is a sales conversation.

how_it_works.text: SHAZAM is member-owned with one vote per member. It joins community banks and credit unions by contact form and publishes no fees.

best_pattern.text: Visa names the sponsored tier on its public licensing page and says who it suits. Its rules state which BIN the Associate may use and who is liable.

discover_today.text: PULSE is the Discover family's route for this segment. Its public site offers a contact form and a five-day portal registration, with participation fees stated in filings but not priced.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers license through the same Principal or Associate path as issuers. Brazil adds a separate merchant acquiring licence.
A member using a VisaNet processor files a regional client information questionnaire first. A non-member processor must sign a VisaNet Letter of Agreement.
Sponsor banks sign the acquiring contract and hold the BIN. The Bancorp and Heartland agreement is a filed example of a Merchant BIN and ICA Sponsorship and Services Agreement.

tools_and_screens.name: Regional client information questionnaire and VisaNet Letter of Agreement
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The documents a member or its processor files before a processor is used.

friction.text: Network standards stop a sponsored acquirer from settling funds itself, which binds it to the sponsor bank.
Processors report that sponsor banks keep wide discretion over their practices and contract terms, and bank alliances supply the sponsorship.
If a portfolio changes hands, the new owner has 10 calendar days to file membership materials or Visa may delete the BINs.

how_it_works.text: An acquirer that wants specialty merchants files the High-Risk License Addendum, form 637. A USD 50,000 annual fee applies from May 2026.
Processors that matter operationally can join as Network Enablement Partners, on a direct NEP Agreement signed within 30 days of designation.
NEP tiers grant test ICAs and BINs.

tools_and_screens.name: NEP Application form
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Submitted to a service provider mailbox. The NEP page names tiers and a contact.

friction.text: Type I processor registration needs form 919, an SSAE 18 or ISAE 3402 report and a continuity form, all sent by email.

how_it_works.text: Acquirer participants sign a Participant Agreement and may operate only in the territory and currency it names.

OptBlue participants must meet launch conditions. These include a Program Agreement, Authorized Processor status matched with Visa and Mastercard, written certification, a financial statement review and a compliance questionnaire.
OptBlue participants then enrol at connect.amex360.com for regulations, training and sales tools.
Processors and gateways register through AMEX Enabled under a click-through NDA, with no fee.
An OptBlue Participant pays a wholesale fee on every charge, set from the Appendix A rate table plus additional fees. Changes need 180 days' notice.

tools_and_screens.name: American Express 360Connect
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: OptBlue regulations, forms, training and bulletins, opened after enrolment is verified.

tools_and_screens.name: AMEX Enabled Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Specifications, product enrolment, DocuSign contracts and up to five extra users.

friction.text: American Express publishes no route for an acquirer to become an OptBlue participant.
Participants may not publish the wholesale fee. Processor pricing guides marked confidential are still posted openly by a bank and a reseller.

how_it_works.text: EASI self-registration covers eighteen company types, including acquirers and acquirer processors. It asks for contacts, a signing authority, company type and regions.
EASI holds specifications, test card kits and a Message Center to network operations.
Acquirers must register High Brand Risk merchants under Discover's HBR programme.

tools_and_screens.name: EASI registration
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A multi-stage form, then credentials by email.

tools_and_screens.name: Partner Resources
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Links to the Release Compliance Tool, Disputes Portal, Developer Center, EASI and Web Merchant Boarding.

friction.text: The EASI Registration Guide PDF returned a server error on 26 September 2026, and Discover publishes no acquirer licensing steps.

best_pattern.text: American Express writes its OptBlue launch conditions as a checklist that a processor can plan against.

discover_today.text: EASI gives acquirers and processors self-service registration that captures signing authority and company type. It opens specifications and test kits, and Discover publishes no licensing steps.

how_it_works.text: The sponsoring acquirer registers the agent in Program Request Management plus regional forms before any service begins.
A senior officer reviews the documents. The member checks finances and principals' backgrounds and inspects the agent's site.
Registration is per acquirer, and from 24 October 2026 US and Canadian members must disclose each agent's numeric IDs and BINs.
Visa Partner now lets agents start registration themselves. They name a sponsor and TPA category and upload a PCI AOC or SAQ D. A Business ID and registry listing follow.
To sponsor payment facilitators an acquirer must meet Visa's risk rating and equity minimums. Visa sends agents to their acquirer and acquirers to their Visa account team.
In 2016 Visa said agents could not register themselves. The current tool reverses that for services that need no sponsor.

tools_and_screens.name: Program Request Management
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The sponsor's registration application for agents and payment facilitators.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Membership Management, 2016
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Predecessor tool on Visa Online, where a payment facilitator's descriptor and BIN went in a free-text comments field.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A public listing with company, regions, services and compliance date. Overdue listings turned yellow, then red, then were removed.

friction.text: The 2016 fee schedule of USD 5,000 per ISO or payment facilitator is the last public figure, and fees are non-refundable after approval.
An agent serving several acquirers is registered separately by each.

how_it_works.text: The sponsoring customer registers the provider in My Company Manager and completes materials within 30 days, and it validates annually.
PCI validation through the Site Data Protection programme must be complete. The customer needs written confirmation before using the provider.
Payment facilitators that submit directly, or serve specialty merchants, must become Network Enablement Partners.
Mastercard publishes the list of registered payment facilitators.

tools_and_screens.name: My Company Manager service provider registration
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where the sponsor registers ISOs and payment facilitators and uploads material.

tools_and_screens.name: Service Provider Categories and PCI matrix
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A public one-page table of provider types and their programme services.

friction.text: Registration fees are billed through MCBS at unpublished amounts.
Missing a registration step can cost the sponsor up to USD 25,000 for each 30 days.

how_it_works.text: A payment facilitator below USD 250 million in American Express volume registers through an OptBlue participant. There is no registration fee.
The participant checks eligibility with its American Express representative first.
For an ISO, the participant runs due diligence and background checks, generates an ISO Registration Number and emails the form to a programme oversight mailbox.
For a payment facilitator, the participant sends a form 30 days before launch. American Express must approve it in writing.
The participant must also run KYC and AML checks and a site visit or name match.
A payfac joining through a Participant takes that Participant's OptBlue price, built from tiers by MCC industry, ticket size, card origin and entry mode.
Fiserv's Fall 2025 guide splits US debit into regulated and unregulated tiers, with regulated debit at 0.04% plus USD 0.25.

tools_and_screens.name: ISO Registration and Certification Form, Appendix F
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A signed certification by the participant plus an ISO list, emailed in.

tools_and_screens.name: Payment Facilitator Registration Form, Appendix G
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: An editable PDF with New, Change or Terminated submission types, an account manager, CAP number, launch date and V/MC registration status.

friction.text: Registration runs on PDFs and a shared mailbox, and no status view is published.
ISOs usually sign merchants on the sponsor's own application, and the sponsor bank co-signs each ISO merchant agreement.

how_it_works.text: Discover tells payment facilitators to register through an acquiring bank in each market. It also advises a money transmitter licence and Level 1 PCI.
ISOs and payment facilitators can self-register on EASI for specifications and test kits.
PULSE participants may sponsor merchants, processors and ISOs and are liable for them.

tools_and_screens.name: EASI
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Self-registration listing ISO and PayFac as company types.

friction.text: Discover publishes no network-level registration step, form or fee for ISOs or payment facilitators.
A former ISO owner says vertical software firms do not know how to structure a sponsor bank relationship, which is the step Discover's guide leaves to them.

best_pattern.text: Visa's registry shows registration and compliance status publicly. Its newer tool lets an agent start registration itself and get a Business ID.

discover_today.text: Discover sends payment facilitators to acquiring banks through a marketing article and lets them self-register on EASI, with no network registration status to see.

by_partner.partner_type: ATM operators (independent deployers and bank fleets)

how_it_works.text: Deployers join as ISO-ATM agents registered by a Visa or Plus client. Key-injection vendors register as Encryption Support Organizations.
In the US the ATM acquirer must do due diligence on each ATM operator, including a site visit or suitable alternative.
Bank examiners describe the chain as sponsor bank approval, a processor contract, and network registration by the sponsor bank.
Members displaying Plus receive a Plus marks licence.

tools_and_screens.name: Program Request Management
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Used to register ISO-ATM agents.

friction.text: Only banks, or processors a bank approves and monitors, may send ATM transactions, so losing a sponsor can halt operations.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers of ATM owners run their own ATM AML monitoring and may join other ATM networks that do not compete.
ATM acquirers join market by market through bank partnerships. There is no global application.
PULSE lists ATM Acquirers as a partner type, promising exclusive Discover and Diners cards. Fees are described only as competitive.

friction.text: Joining runs through a contact page.

best_pattern.text: Bank examiners define the ATM ISO chain in one sentence: sponsor bank approval, processor contract, and network registration by the bank.

discover_today.text: PULSE pitches ATM acquirers on card access with no published joining steps or rates.

how_it_works.text: Fintech Fast Track asks for a registered corporation, new to issuing, with at least USD 3 million raised. Visa and the enablement partner both review.
Non-bank and crypto issuers file a Core Product Program Information Form and need Visa's written approval.
Visa describes the sponsor bank model of BIN sponsor, processor and programme manager.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Partner programme catalogue
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Fast Track, licensing, third-party registration and the PIF.

how_it_works.text: Since May 2025 a Principal needs Mastercard's approval to act as BIN sponsor for a sponsored programme manager, and approval is revocable without notice.
Product Express sells issuance through pre-certified partners and BIN sponsorship.
In the UK, BIN Sponsor Plus accredits sponsors that commit to higher training and due diligence.

tools_and_screens.name: Engage portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: An online application, product qualification, franchise screening, IDs and an agreement.

how_it_works.text: The Agile Partner Platform connects fintechs to sponsor banks and processors such as i2c, Lithic and Marqeta. American Express says it is selective.

friction.text: The fintech page offers no application or eligibility information.

how_it_works.text: Discover assembles BIN sponsors, processors and programme managers for fintechs and names no fast-track programme.

friction.text: Stripe, Adyen, Lithic and Highnote document issuing on Visa and Mastercard, and none documents Discover issuing.

best_pattern.text: Visa publishes Fast Track eligibility criteria and review stages that a founder can check before applying.

discover_today.text: Discover describes a sponsor ecosystem for fintechs without eligibility, steps or named partners.

how_it_works.text: Visa Ready runs six steps from creating a Visa Partner account to a directory listing.
Visa Developer credentials beyond sandbox need a signed contract, collected in an Onboarding Dashboard.

tools_and_screens.name: Onboarding Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Business entity, contacts, project, environment request, users and credentials.

friction.text: Onboarding can take two weeks or several months.

how_it_works.text: Company verification links a Connect profile or company ID, or routes to due diligence with a reference number.

tools_and_screens.name: Customer Onboarding Platform questionnaire
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Triggered when a company adds a Business Relationship Type.

how_it_works.text: AMEX Enabled is three steps: register the company under an NDA, enrol a Knowledge Base user, then use the dashboard. There is no fee.

tools_and_screens.name: AMEX Enabled Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Messaging Center, product enrolment and DocuSign contracts.

how_it_works.text: The Developer Center is invite-only, starting from a Contact Us form.

tools_and_screens.name: EASI
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Self-registration for eighteen company types.

friction.text: Two different doors apply, invite-only for APIs and self-service for specifications.

best_pattern.text: AMEX Enabled makes provider joining a free, three-step self-service flow with digital contracts.

discover_today.text: EASI is self-service while the Developer Center needs an invitation.

how_it_works.text: US merchants either sign directly with American Express or go through an OptBlue provider that sets the rate.
OptBlue merchants see a Participant's price. The Participant must tell them that it, not American Express, sets the cost of acceptance.
Merchants enable Discover through their acquirer, found on a find-an-acquirer page.

best_pattern.text: American Express offers two published routes, direct or through an OptBlue provider.

design_moves.title: One join map per partner type
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions (sponsored or associate)
ATM operators (independent deployers and bank fleets)
design_moves.move: Open the partner portal with a chooser by partner type. Each path states who signs, whether a sponsor is needed, the documents asked for and the identifiers issued at approval.
design_moves.why_advantage: Only Visa publishes the steps for a direct licence. American Express hands over rules only after signing, and Discover routes every type to a contact form.

design_moves.title: A sponsor console for third-party registration
partner_types: ATM operators (independent deployers and bank fleets)
design_moves.move: Give the sponsoring bank one registration record per ISO, payment facilitator or ATM deployer. It holds the diligence checklist, PCI evidence and identifiers, with a visible status up to written approval.
design_moves.why_advantage: American Express takes these registrations as emailed PDFs and Mastercard takes them in My Company Manager. Sponsor staff track the work in Excel, and Discover publishes no network step.

design_moves.title: A welcome record of identifiers
design_moves.move: At approval, show one record with the IIN or BIN ranges, participant numbers, settlement parameters and directory entries. Keep the same record live as ranges change.
design_moves.why_advantage: Rivals issue these through several tools and deadlines. Visa uses a UVID, then a Business ID, then a directory entry due within 10 business days, and American Express assigns ranges during pre-launch support.

design_moves.title: Named roles captured once at joining
design_moves.move: Collect the signing authority, senior officer, operations lead and portal administrator in the first form, and reuse them for access, bulletins and escalation.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa, Mastercard and American Express each define such roles but collect them in separate directories after launch. EASI already asks for a signing authority at registration.

design_moves.title: Service levels on the network's own steps
design_moves.move: State the network's response time for credentials, registration review and reconsideration of a refusal, and show it on each step.
design_moves.why_advantage: Elo publishes a five-day reconsideration window and PULSE a five-day credential promise. The study found no licensing timeline from Visa, Mastercard or American Express.

design_moves.title: Say plainly what joining costs
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions (sponsored or associate)
design_moves.move: Publish registration and participation fees, or state that a step carries no fee, on the join map.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa's last public agent fee is from 2016, Mastercard's sit behind Connect, and PULSE states participation fees exist without amounts. American Express states that OptBlue payment facilitator and AMEX Enabled registration carry no fee. OptBlue forbids Participants to publish the wholesale fee, yet Fiserv and First Data guides listing every tier sit openly on bank and reseller sites.

design_moves.title: A public registry with live status
design_moves.move: List registered payment facilitators, ISOs and certified providers with their compliance status, so merchants and sponsors can check them.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa's registry shows compliance status and Mastercard lists registered payment facilitators. Discover's Partner Directory lists type-approved products only.

design_moves.title: Carry one application record forward
design_moves.move: Pre-fill later onboarding tasks from what the partner gave at registration, so EASI data flows into Going Live stages.
design_moves.why_advantage: UnionPay's public guide describes pre-filled onboarding tasks. Discover today runs separate doors for EASI, the Developer Center and the Partner Product Portal.

unseen.why: Visa's last public figures are from 2016 and Mastercard points to its gated billing centre.
